findings.title: Slots inside a date override skip the busy-time check entirely
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, once a slot is found to be on a day with a date override and inside the override window, the function returns `true` immediately (`if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }`) without ever evaluating the `busy` array. This means that for fixed hosts (the primary path this PR adds, where `checkIfIsAvailable` is the only busy-time filter), any existing booking or calendar busy time that falls inside a date-override window will be reported as available. The attendee can be shown (and attempt to book) a slot where the host already has a meeting. The override should restrict the time window, not bypass conflict checking.

findings.title: Working-hours check compares UTC slot minutes against organizer-timezone working hours
findings.body: In the new working-hours validation inside `checkIfIsAvailable`, `slotStartTime` is a UTC dayjs, so `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` yields minutes since midnight UTC. But `workingHour.startTime/endTime` (from `getUserAvailability` / `getAggregateWorkingHours`) are minutes since midnight in the organizer's timezone. For any organizer not in UTC (e.g. Asia/Kolkata in the test data, working hours 09:30–18:00 local), the comparison `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` uses the wrong clock, wrongly marking valid in-hours slots as unavailable or letting out-of-hours slots through. Additionally, `const end` is computed identically to `const start` (both from `slotStartTime`), so the `end > workingHour.endTime` condition never tests the slot's end time — the event length is not accounted for at all.

findings.title: Date overrides that cross midnight in the invitee timezone are silently dropped
findings.body: The new override computation converts the override start/end to minutes since midnight in the invitee timezone (`dayjs(...).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...minute()`). `hour()` wraps at 24, so an override such as 23:00–01:00 (invitee time) produces `startTime: 1380, endTime: 60`. `buildSlots` then skips this timeframe via the `if (start >= end) continue;` guard, so the override disappears entirely instead of splitting into two ranges. The previous code had the same wrap problem, but this rewrite was the opportunity to fix it; users with overnight overrides will see their normal working hours applied (or no availability) instead of the override.

findings.title: Object-identity comparison makes the unavailability-override check dead code
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the check `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two freshly created dayjs objects with `===`, which is always false regardless of the underlying times. The intent (per the surrounding logic) was to detect a zero-length override, i.e. an override marking the whole day unavailable (start === end). Such 'blocked day' overrides will not be recognized by this branch; instead they fall through to the subsequent `slotEndTime.isBefore(...)` checks, which for an empty range will mark every slot as outside the override and the day will incorrectly become unavailable (or available depending on order) — in any case the special-cased behavior can never trigger and is dead code.

findings.title: Override-day matching compares organizer-local date against UTC slot date
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") === slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` compares the organizer-local calendar date of the override start with the UTC calendar date of the slot. For organizers in non-UTC timezones, slots in the first hours of a UTC day (or last hours) belong to a different local day, so the override-day detection is off by one day for those slots. Slots just after midnight UTC on the override day will not be treated as override-day slots (and vice versa), producing wrong availability at day boundaries.

findings.title: No test for the fixed-host date override in a round-robin team event
findings.body: The PR's headline fix is that date overrides of fixed hosts are respected in round-robin events (issue #8207), but the added test only covers a single-user event with a date override and a different invitee timezone. There is no test with a ROUND_ROBIN event containing an `isFixed` host with a date override plus a non-fixed host, so the main code path added in `getSchedule` (`fixedHosts.every(...)` with date overrides) and the buggy busy-time bypass it introduces are not exercised by any test.

findings.title: DST offset computed once from override start may be wrong for override end
findings.body: The offset applied to the override is derived from a single instant (`override.start`): `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`. If the override range spans a DST transition (possible for multi-hour or multi-day overrides), the end time is shifted by the start instant's offset, misplacing the end of the availability window by the DST delta. The offset should be evaluated at the respective instant for both start and end.
